note: First hypotheses, from open coding 300 posts. Each one gets tested on the full coded corpus, not on this sample.

hypotheses.statement: The pains people mention most now come after the code is written (review, QA, CI, the cleanup of AI-written code), not during writing.
hypotheses.disproved_if: Codes for the writing stage (unclear-requirements, design-drift, interruptions) together appear in at least as many relevant posts as review-overload + test-ci-friction + qa-capacity + ai-output-quality + bottleneck-shift.

hypotheses.statement: Complaints about review overload and the bottleneck moving have grown over the window, alongside AI coding.
hypotheses.disproved_if: The share of relevant posts coded review-overload or bottleneck-shift is flat or falling across the window's quarters (no upward slope beyond noise).

hypotheses.statement: Non-engineers depending on engineering (the Blast Radius candidate) is a minor pain in this data.
hypotheses.disproved_if: eng-dependency is among the 8 most common codes. Note: HN mostly reflects engineers' views, so this must be rechecked on PM and design sources before it can rule anything out.

hypotheses.statement: When people say a small change broke something, it's usually because the change had effects nobody could see (change-impact), not because the edit itself was wrong.
hypotheses.disproved_if: Among relevant posts about something breaking, wrong-edit explanations outnumber change-impact ones.

hypotheses.statement: Of the pains people discuss, the ones agents fit best are review overload, QA capacity and AI missing the team's context. Each is multi-step, uses several tools, and a human can check the result.
hypotheses.disproved_if: Scored at Stage 2, none of these three ranks in the top 5 on agent fit.
